sections.title: Profile
sections.text: Ripresa, manager of a well-known orchestra in Nuova Volsinii who contacted us after observing that many with positions of power in the city have ties to Rhodes Island, in the hope of increasing exposure for her orchestra. She participates in certain field missions at her own request.

sections.title: Clinical Analysis
sections.text:
Imaging tests show the indistinct outlines of internal organs, obscured by abnormal shadows. Originium granules detected in the circulatory system. The subject is confirmed to be infected with Oripathy.

[Cell-Originium Assimilation] 6%
A small distribution of Originium crystals is present on Operator Ripresa's thigh.

[Blood Originium-Crystal Density] 0.25u/L
Operator Ripresa contracted Originium at a young age. Her condition is currently under control.

sections.title: Archive File 1
sections.text:
Czerny had had enough. For the fourth time, Ripresa had given him a new tape after her piano lesson.
The first, a piano etude, could be justified as homework, but the next was a trombone solo, followed by an oboe and bassoon duet. This one was apparently the percussion section from a symphony movement. Ripresa was a motivated student, a quick study, and diligent with her practice. Other students in the studio said she must be a huge fan of Professor Czerny, and at one point Czerny would have agreed.
'Did you need something from me, Frau Liesel?'
'Oh, um... I've always been very interested in your compositional style...'
'That's not what I'm talking about. You've taken enough of my lessons to be familiar with my style, and I've heard enough of your tapes to get a feel for them. I must certainly compliment you on your choice of repertoire. Now, what do you want from me?'
Ripresa blinked for a few seconds before taking out a few video tapes from her bag.
'Well, Maestro Czerny, these are recordings of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra's performances, a small chamber orchestra of around twenty members that I currently direct...'
Ripresa's description gave Czerny food for thought. He recalled his most recent schedule to check whether he had time to make a trip to Nuova Volsinii. A Leithanian orchestra? What sort of chemistry could he form with them as a pianist? Czerny cleared his throat, interrupting Ripresa's monologue.
'I would be happy to work with your orchestra—'
'Really?! Thank you! About the composition's style—our members agreed that we would prefer a hopeful work to a melancholic one. With Maestro Czerny writing it, I'm sure our performance will deliver hope to our listeners' hearts!'
'...Composition?'
Czerny swallowed the words 'performing as a pianist' as Ripresa continued to describe her request. Her ideas for the new composition were very specific, and the recordings were sufficiently vivid that a melody gradually took form in his mind as she spoke.

Czerny's new work was unsurprisingly a massive hit in Nuova Volsinii at its premiere by the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra. We deliberated on whether to tell Ripresa that she could simply come forward with any requests she has, without resorting to her old negotiation tactics from Nuova Volsinii. But she seems to enjoy the process very much. Perhaps it is not such a bad thing after all, to let her do things her way.

sections.title: Archive File 2
sections.text:
Certain strange rumors came to our attention as HR performed its background check on Operator Ripresa. When we inquired with Operator Bellone on this, he simply smiled and said, 'She's good to her famiglia.'
The theater that the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra had partnered with was closed for investigation following the murder of the musician Paola Memminger, forcing the orchestra to seek out other venues in Nuova Volsinii.
Their agreement with the new theater was initially only a temporary lease, but extra costs were incurred as rehearsals intensified, which were borne by the venue under the rental agreement. Meanwhile, the orchestra would have difficulty finding a new venue on short notice if the agreement were terminated, locking the two parties in a stalemate.
Rather than avoid the issue, Ripresa set about reviewing rehearsal records and expenses incurred, putting together a list of the extra costs and incorporating them into their budget in her capacity as the orchestra's representative. It was not an easy decision for an orchestra in transition, and Ripresa had to redistribute a budget that was already tight to begin with, incurring additional risks in the process, but she decided to take on the expense knowing that the orchestra risked more than monetary loss if the partnership were terminated.
In interviews, HR learned that the venue was surprised by her decision.
It kept the partnership intact, and the two sides began negotiations on future billing and usage. While a stable long-term partnership is as yet uncertain, the pressing issues have been resolved without escalation, as Ripresa has consistently done in any matter involving the orchestra's interests.
At the end of the investigation, we were still unable to clearly define her actions. She did not seem to be trying to expand her influence, but rather appeared to take on responsibility for any issue as a matter of habit, acting less like a representative and more like a...
'That petite Caprinae resolved the conflict between the vicious foreigners and our famiglia like the Godmother!'
While inputting the data, the investigator could not help but recall certain rumors from the early stages of the investigation.

sections.title: Archive File 3
sections.text:
One consistent theme from our interviews with members of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra was that many of them had begun to identify themselves as Nuova Volsinians, or more specifically as 'members of the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra of Nuova Volsinii'.
Most of them came to Siracusa as exiles from Leithanien, harboring both bitterness towards Leithanien and wariness towards Siracusa. They struggled in Siracusa's cities despite their talents in music and Arts, and many even gave up on music. After all, music that was rejected by Leithanien would not necessarily fare much better in Siracusa. It was only when Paola Memminger brought them together that they finally found their home.
After her death, the members faced uncertainty about more than just personnel or venue, but also about their own futures. They mentioned that, for the first time, they were faced with the reality that without a steady anchor holding it all together, they could dissolve and scatter at any moment. Leaving was always a realistic option.
Things changed when Ripresa took over.
She did not attempt to define the orchestra's identity, nor did she emphasize to its members what they ought to represent. She simply performed the duties that seemed mundane, but were very important: ensuring that rehearsals continued on schedule, checking the details of their rental agreements with venues, and making contingency plans to avoid potential conflict. As things began to settle down, something changed subtly in the mentality of the members, nudging them towards putting down roots in the city. The members offered various answers when we asked the reason, but they all pointed to the same thing: Liesel was here, and she would conduct them tomorrow.
Notably, this shift in identity did not come from any clear gesture of acceptance by the city, but from the orchestra itself. For its members, 'Schwarzervorhang' was no longer just a collection of musicians, but a community they lived in, one in which they did not have to explain where they came from, nor constantly prepare for where to go next.
For what was perhaps the first time since they left Leithanien, the people who came together because of Paola had a home, one that they did not need to check on constantly, and one that was not easily lost. All thanks to the leadership of Paola's foster daughter.

sections.title: Archive File 4
sections.text:
'I was sitting in the gallery when the Caprinae who killed Mama Paola was sentenced by Judge Lavinia. He stood there with an impassive expression and freely admitted his crime. To him, she was a stranger—no more than a symbol, one that was incompatible with the narrative he believed in. For a long time after the trial, I had a hard time accepting the whole thing.
'She never preached sedition the way the killer said she did. She didn't gather us to oppose anything. From the beginning, all she told me and the other members was that we should tell the truth, not be afraid, and enjoy the music we love... I just don't understand how it turned out this way. I don't understand, so I need to do something.
'Revenge? Oh, not at all! The case is closed, and the culprit has received his punishment. The other members are all of the same mind on this. What I feel I must do is... well, maybe it's an impulsive act, but I feel like Mama Paola did nothing wrong, nor did anybody in the orchestra. I don't want anyone to have to change their way of life just because someone else doesn't like it. We'll continue to live this way. In fact, we'll live even freer and let the Leithanians suffer on their own. We'll play the music we want to play, and only the music we want to play.
If you ask me whether I have a grudge against the killer... he took my mother from me and hurt my family. Of course I have a grudge. But I won't let him or people like him ruin my life. I think that's what she would have wanted.'

[Classified Log]
Grimmacht's voice is silent. The shadow of Gaul appears in the clouds. Ewigegnade is cleansing Leithanien of all disharmony, and her iron fists reach beyond the borders of Leithanien. Rhodes Island must be vigilant, and consider its next move carefully.

sections.title: Promotion Record
sections.text:
Maestro Czerny,
I hope this letter finds you well.
I apologize for not being able to visit you personally, as I have been busy with the Schwarzervorhang Orchestra's performances lately. I am writing today to share with you some changes that have happened recently, and ask something of you.
Yesterday, I ran into a Caprinae at the end of her wits holding an instrument case, saying that she came from Leithanien to Nuova Volsinii, just like the other members that Mama Paola recruited. I didn't understand a lot of what she said, but I feel there must be many people like Mama Paola who couldn't play the music they wanted to back home. This woman really loved the piece you wrote for us, and so I asked her to stay as second violist.
You may have already guessed what I want to ask... We already have a violist, but I wanted her to stay, and to give her a place in that piece that belongs to her.
I know you wrote it for our particular orchestra, which is why I didn't want her to just play in unison with the other violist—it would make her feel redundant, not to mention that the performance would deviate from your original concept. I want the composition to truly respond to her, just as it did for the others, but I'm not Mama Paola, and I'm still learning the art of composition.
So I would like to ask if you could make some arrangements to the piece, so that the second violist has a distinct and unique significance. Whether it be the voicing, the structure, or anything else you see fit, I am willing to put my full faith in whatever you decide.
Actually, she doesn't yet know that we're inviting her to stay... I was shadowing her before writing this letter, and I saw her go to a music store to ask about selling her instrument. Please, I don't want her to give up music! I'll try to get her to perform with us until you write back.
I look forward to your reply!
Liesel
